elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits an assignment by Client to an affiliate without the other party's approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment by Client to a successor in a merger without approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment by Client to a successor in an acquisition without approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment by Client to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets without approval.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink remains subject to the baseline prohibition on assignment or transfer without Client's prior written approval; the exception applies only to Client.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign or transfer the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that TrueLink shall not assign or transfer the Agreement to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment exception contains no written-notice requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: There is no successor exception for TrueLink; TrueLink remains subject to Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice mechanism for a TrueLink successor assignment is included.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Client assignments to affiliates are also exempt from consent, even though an affiliate assignment need not be a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness limitation applies only to Client's approval of a TrueLink assignment, not to TrueLink's approval of a Client assignment.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink has no assignment exception and therefore remains subject to Client's prior written approval for such assignments.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: The clause generally states that Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld, subject to the separate absolute prohibition on assignments to Client competitors.

result.reason: The operative redline satisfies every preferred requirement: it gives Client the specified affiliate and successor carve-outs, retains consent control over TrueLink assignments with a reasonableness standard, prohibits competitor assignments, and eliminates any TrueLink termination right arising from Client's change of control. It does not satisfy the fallback because it lacks mutual successor rights and written-notice duties and does not apply a reasonableness standard to TrueLink's consent to Client assignments. The changes are narrowly directed to the preferred position and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
